mechanism_posthoc.finding_2: yet burial persists: at w=2, 6/9 hard cells have ZERO window pairs in the optimizer's global fold but 5 of them are still AUG/Kozak-buried by the JunctionEvaluator metric (isolated 40-nt fragment fold, utr5[-20:]+cds[:20])
mechanism_posthoc.finding_3: root cause = metric/optimizer context mismatch: the C++ penalty suppresses window pairs in the full-construct CKY fold, while the accessibility metric folds the isolated 40-nt junction fragment, where the CDS-terminal 20 nt self-hairpins (j1 structures show intra-fragment pairs over the AUG region even when global window pairs = 0)
mechanism_posthoc.finding_4: stability cost is NOT reduced vs P1 (median 0.015-0.031/nt across weights vs P1 v1 median 0.0220; threshold 0.011) — integrating the junction term at design time did not tame the global stability cost either
mechanism_posthoc.finding_5: CAI criterion passes trivially (median delta_cai ~ -0.06, i.e. designed CAI IMPROVED ~0.06 over the RNARL-derived serial baselines at lambda=2.0)
mechanism_posthoc.conclusion: repairing fragment-fold accessibility requires the penalty to act on the fragment-fold objective itself (or on intra-window self-structure), not on the global-construct fold; a larger w_jun cannot fix a metric the optimizer does not see
